## Stinknet - CAPLTER

Central Arizona Phoenix Long-Term Ecological Research, <https://globalfutures.asu.edu/caplter/>

Purpose: Find the microclimatic and chemical impacts on the growth of stinknet in the Phoenix metropolitan area.

"ammonT","ammonB", "nitrT","nitrB", "phosT","phosB", "pH", "conduct", "bulkdens","ocarbT", "ocarbB", "ONCPIL", "clay","sand" (out of 100)

Organic Carbon, pH - AA, Conductivity - AB \>1 is really salty, Bulk Density - AG,

<https://uw.pressbooks.pub/appliedmultivariatestatistics/chapter/anosim/>

```{r}
### Libraries and data cleaning ###

#Libraries
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(stringr)
library(janitor)
library(tidyr)
library(vegan)

#dataset
data <- read_excel("/Users/elise/OneDrive/Documents/Desktop/Global Futures research/Cleaned_Data.xlsx")
#View(data) 
#str(df)

data[c("cnT","cnB")]<-sapply(data[c("cnT","cnB")],as.numeric)
data[data<0] <- 0
## round numbers in the columns clay-phosB
df <- data %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 3))

## remove empty rows
df <- na.omit(df)
#head(df)

```

```{r}
## Filter data based on Stinknet="TRUE" (sn_true)

#df <- df %>% mutate(T_ONCPIL = (df[df$ONCPIL == "TRUE", ])
#head(df)
##or turn into seperate column

df_true <- df[df$ONCPIL == "TRUE", ]
df_false <- df[df$ONCPIL == "FALSE", ]
```

```{r}
#average Amounts of nutrients in the soils where Sinknet is found

sn_nutrient <- df_true[,c("ammonT","ammonB",
                   "nitrT","nitrB",
                   "phosT","phosB")]
nutrient_averages <- colMeans(sn_nutrient)
print(nutrient_averages,3)
```

```{r}
## Contigency table of urban and stinknet ##
snur_df = data.frame(df$urban,df$ONCPIL)
snur_df = table(df$urban,df$ONCPIL) 
                
print(snur_df) #Where Urban: 0/1 and Stinknet: T/F

## chi squared test
print(chisq.test(snur_df))

# p-value: is over 0.05 (NH) stinknet rate is independent from the rate of urbanization in the dataset
# x-squared: difference between expected count and true count  if NH is TRUE
##bigger number means larger distance between NH and observed values
# df: degrees of freedom, critical value

####

# mosiac plot spread of stinknet presence and status of urban scenery 
ggplot(df, aes(x = urban, fill = ONCPIL)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Stinknet occurences in Urban/Non Urban areas",
       x = "Urban 0/1",
       y = "Count",
       fill = "Stinknet")
```

```{r}
#-------------------NMDS-----------------------------------------------

#create dataset:
sndf <-df[,c("ammonT","ammonB", "nitrT","nitrB", "phosT","phosB", "pH",
            "conduct", "bulkdens","ocarbT", "ocarbB", "ONCPIL", "clay","sand")]


#In the structure of [c(rows),c(columns)] wanted in the dataset.

#COLUMNS: such that the dataset includes only the columns with the needed metadata 
##(treatments, sites, etc.) and the actual species being analyzed.



#Then break into metadata and species data (AFTER remove rows/NAs):
SN<-sndf[,"ONCPIL"] #stinknet t/f

SOILSPECIE <-sndf[,c("clay","sand")] #different chemistry (soil)



#run NMDS:

Ord1<-metaMDS(SOILSPECIE, wascores=TRUE, k=3) #relationship between specie and site
Ord1

#And record stress from results.
#wascores designates to use the weighted average for species scores.

#Can specify the number of dimensions with k to get the stress to an acceptable level. Can remove that part of the command if don't need to specify.



#Plot the NMDS in R: 

library(ggplot2)

plot(Ord1)

#colfactorn<-factor(META$Treat)
colfactorn<-factor(SN$ONCPIL)  ##ask about this, create two coulumns? one for t and f?

#Change names in the code above for the name of the metadata set and the treatment of interest to color the points.

points(Ord1, display="sites",cex=1, pch=16, col=c(1,4,3,2)[colfactorn])

text(Ord1, display="Soil Type", cex=1)

ordiellipse(Ord1, colfactorn, col=c(1,4,3,2), kind="ehull", lwd=3)

legend(x="topleft", legend=levels(colfactorn), col=c(1,4,3,2), pch=16)



#Extract scores to plot in Excel:

print(scores(SoilOrd1, display="sites"))

print(scores(SoilOrd1, display="species"))



#Running post hoc pairwise comparisons:

#Turn site scores into a dataset:

MDS1 = Ord1$points[,1]

MDS2 = Ord1$points[,2]

Ord1XY = data.frame(MDS1 = MDS1, MDS2 = MDS2)

print(Ord1XY)



#Choose post hoc test of interest:

#Change names in the code for the name of the metadata set (META) and the treatment (Treat) of interest.

#ANOSIM:

#summary(anosim(Ord1XY, META$Treat1))
summary(anosim(Ord1XY, SN$ONCPIL))

#or PERMANOVA:

#print(adonis(Ord1XY~Treat1*Treat2, META))
print(adonis2(Ord1XY~ONCPIL, SN))

#with post hoc pairwise PERMANOVA if a treatment is significant (have to do each treatment separately):

library(RVAideMemoire)

pairwise.perm.manova(DistRESULTS, META$Treat1)

pairwise.perm.manova(DistRESULTS, META$Treat2)



#----------Distance matrix instead of NMDS of raw data--------------------



#Create distance matrix:

DistRESULTS<-vegdist(SPECIES)



#And then run PERMANOVA on it:

print(adonis(DistRESULTS~Treat1*Treat2, META))

#Followed by pairwise comparisons of treatment levels if significant (have to do each treatment separately):

library(RVAideMemoire)

pairwise.perm.manova(DistRESULTS, META$Treat1) 

pairwise.perm.manova(DistRESULTS, META$Treat2) 

#ord ellipse
```
